results.description:
At our company Christmas party, in front of four hundred people, my husband thanked his CFO for making the year possible. Then he thanked me for my patience.

The room laughed. That night I found the email where Gideon Thorne called our four-year marriage a sunk cost, something he'd write off once his billion-dollar deal closed.

On Christmas Eve I asked him if we were all right. He told me we were fully covered.

So I left my ring on the dining table, packed one suitcase and a green tin box, and drove the twenty-two minutes to my father's house.

Gideon has spent his whole life making sure nothing can cost him. He's never asked who owns the ground his family's tower stands on. It was my great-grandfather's. The lease he signed in 1932 runs out on the first of April, and the person who decides whether it's renewed is me.

There's one clause in it, written by a man who hated bankers. Whoever wants the lease renewed comes alone, in person, and sits at my kitchen table. I've made it Tuesdays.

I'd put it at ten percent he lasts until spring.

The Wife He Wrote Off is a steamy standalone billionaire marriage-in-crisis romance with a secret heiress, a Christmas Eve walkout, a CFO with plans of her own, a long and very public grovel, and a guaranteed HEA. No cheating. A standalone novel set in the world of The Quiet Heiresses.
